boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Dinwiddie Court House record (March 31, 1865) in the Appomattox Campaign [March-April 1865]. White Oak Road (VA087) is the same day; Five Forks (VA088) follows on April 1. Army-wide returns, campaign-wide loss and prisoner totals, the April 9 paroles and the retreat as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force text reads 65,277 (US 45,247; CS 20,030) and the live field zero. Humphreys gives, from the February 20 return, 5,760 enlisted men in the two Lees' cavalry divisions (including Roberts's brigade) and about 3,600 of Pickett's and 3,000 of Johnson's infantry (6,600) for the five brigades at Five Forks, and the present for duty of Sheridan's enlisted cavalry as 13,000; Fitzhugh Lee says Pickett came up with five small brigades of infantry.
claims.rationale: The frozen figures state no date or population. Humphreys' Confederate figures are February 20 return strengths assigned to the formations present, not counts on March 31; the Union cavalry figure is a campaign-opening present-for-duty total. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory; NPS says the Confederates drove the Union vanguard back, temporarily stalling Sheridan, and that Pickett withdrew before daybreak to Five Forks. Fitzhugh Lee says they drove the Union cavalry to within half a mile of the Court House and began moving back to Five Forks at daylight; Humphreys says the Gibbs-Gregg attack forced Pickett to face about and meet Sheridan's line in front of the Court House in a contest that lasted until night.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Pickett's withdrawal on the morning of April 1 belongs to the interval before VA088.

open_questions: Sheridan's report and March 31 dispatch (selected; cited under VA088 and VA096) are not used here under the three-family ceiling, nor is Lee's April 1 letter relaying Pickett's report (selected; cited under VA089 only for its April 1 prisoners from the Twenty-fourth Corps). Pickett's own report was not inspected. Crook's, Merritt's, Custer's and Davies's reports (Nos. 200, 203, 208, 209) and the Warren Court of Inquiry record remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the commander of the Second Corps in this campaign, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; where it narrates his own corps it is a participant's account. It relies on the reports of Sheridan, Warren, Wright, Gibbon, Ewell and Fitzhugh Lee, on Confederate testimony before the Warren Court of Inquiry and on the returns, so it is not independent of those families. Lee's, Sheridan's, Bushrod Johnson's, Miles's, Gibbon's, Ewell's and Fitzhugh Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XLVI, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
